### Related Patterns

**Prerequisites (Must implement before SDK):**

- **API Gateway Pattern (PTN-TECH-APIGW-001):** SDKs integrate with API Gateway for centralized authentication, rate limiting, request routing. Gateway provides OAuth token endpoint for SDK authentication, enforces rate limits SDK resilience modules handle, routes SDK requests to backend services.

- **OpenAPI Specification Standard (STD-DOC-OPENAPI-001):** SDK generation requires comprehensive OpenAPI 3.0 specifications as single source-of-truth. Design-first API approach creates OpenAPI spec before implementation, enabling SDK generation from day one.

**Complementary Patterns (Enhance SDK capabilities):**

- **OAuth 2.0 Authentication Pattern (PTN-SEC-API-005):** SDKs implement OAuth 2.0 client credentials flow for service-to-service authentication. Authentication module handles token acquisition, caching, refresh, secure credential storage.

- **API Versioning Pattern (PTN-APP-API-020):** SDK versioning aligned with API versioning strategy. SDK major version matches API major version (Claims API v2.x → claims-sdk 2.y.z). Semantic versioning communicates breaking changes.

- **Circuit Breaker Pattern (PTN-APP-API-006):** SDK resilience modules implement circuit breaker preventing cascade failures. Circuit opens after consecutive failures, fails fast during outages, half-opens for health checks.

- **Distributed Tracing Pattern (PTN-INFRA-EVT-004):** SDKs propagate trace context (W3C Trace-Context headers) enabling end-to-end tracing. SDK emits spans for API calls enabling latency analysis and dependency mapping.

- **API Monitoring Pattern (PTN-INFRA-EVT-003):** SDK observability modules emit metrics (request count, latency, error rate) consumed by monitoring systems. SDK version tracking enables correlating issues with SDK releases.

**Alternative Approaches:**

- **GraphQL Schema SDL Pattern (PTN-APP-GRAPHQL-001):** For GraphQL APIs, use GraphQL Schema Definition Language (SDL) + code generation tools (Apollo Codegen, GraphQL Code Generator) instead of OpenAPI + OpenAPI Generator. Similar principles apply: schema-first development, automated code generation, multi-language SDKs.

- **gRPC Service Definition Pattern (PTN-APP-GRPC-001):** For gRPC APIs, use Protocol Buffers (.proto files) + Protocol Compiler (protoc) generating language-specific SDKs. gRPC provides native SDK generation, binary serialization (more efficient than JSON REST), bidirectional streaming.

### Dependencies

**Required Infrastructure:**

- **API Gateway Infrastructure (STD-INFRA-APIGW-001):** Production API Gateway (Kong, Apigee, AWS API Gateway) providing authentication enforcement, rate limiting, request routing. SDKs depend on gateway OAuth endpoints and standard HTTP semantics.

- **CI/CD Pipeline Infrastructure (STD-INFRA-CICD-001):** Automated build pipeline supporting multi-language builds (Java/Maven, Python/pip, JavaScript/npm, .NET/NuGet, Go modules). Matrix builds for parallel language compilation.

- **Package Registry Access (STD-INFRA-PKGREG-001):** Accounts and credentials for package registries: Maven Central (Sonatype OSSRH), PyPI, npm organization, NuGet, GitHub (Go modules). Publishing automation via CI/CD.

**Required Standards:**

- **API Design Standard (STD-API-DESIGN-001):** RESTful API conventions (resource naming, HTTP methods, status codes) ensuring consistent SDK generation. APIs must follow standard patterns for SDK generation to produce idiomatic code.

- **OpenAPI Specification Standard (STD-DOC-OPENAPI-001):** All APIs documented in OpenAPI 3.0 format with comprehensive schemas, examples, error definitions. OpenAPI quality directly impacts SDK quality.

- **Semantic Versioning Standard (STD-GOV-SEMVER-001):** API and SDK versioning following semantic versioning (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Breaking changes require MAJOR version increment communicated clearly to SDK users.

- **Security Standards (STD-SEC-*):** OAuth 2.0 standard for authentication, TLS 1.2+ for encryption, secure credential storage (environment variables, secret managers), vulnerability scanning (Snyk, Dependabot).

## TL;DR

**Problem:** Organizations building platform APIs lack standardized Software Development Kits (SDKs), forcing consuming teams to build custom HTTP clients taking weeks per integration with inconsistent quality, resulting in significant engineering time spent on integration support, high support ticket volumes, poor developer experience, slow partner onboarding, and lost opportunities from delayed or abandoned integrations.

**Solution:** Implement comprehensive SDK development framework using automated code generation from OpenAPI specifications producing production-grade SDKs across multiple languages (Java, Python, JavaScript, .NET, Go) with idiomatic wrappers, OAuth 2.0 authentication, retry logic, circuit breakers, and comprehensive documentation, distributed via standard package managers (Maven Central, PyPI, npm, NuGet) enabling rapid integrations.

**When to Use:**
- Platform APIs consumed by external partners, customers, or third-party developers requiring easy integration
- Internal microservices architecture with 10+ services needing service-to-service communication
- Multi-language client requirements (3+ programming languages) across consuming teams
- Complex authentication (OAuth 2.0, JWT, mutual TLS) and error handling requiring consistent implementation
- Rapid API evolution requiring backward compatibility and version management
- Developer experience as a differentiator for partner adoption

**Key Benefits:**
- Significant integration time reduction (from weeks of custom client work to days with SDK)
- Improved developer satisfaction (SDK-enabled platforms consistently outperform documentation-only approaches)
- Substantially reduced support burden through built-in error handling and diagnostics
- Higher platform adoption and API usage from lower integration barriers
- Consistency enforcement (authentication, retry logic, error handling) across all integrations
- Faster API evolution with semantic versioning and backward compatibility
- Reduced duplicate code across integration points
- Better observability with distributed tracing and SDK version tracking

**Implementation Complexity:** Medium-High (2-3 engineers, 8-12 weeks for initial multi-language SDK, ongoing maintenance)

**Prerequisites:** OpenAPI 3.0 specifications for all APIs, code generation tools (OpenAPI Generator), package registry accounts (Maven Central, PyPI, npm, NuGet), CI/CD infrastructure supporting multi-language builds, dedicated SDK development team with multi-language proficiency, API Gateway infrastructure for authentication and rate limiting.

**Related Patterns:** API Gateway Pattern (PTN-TECH-APIGW-001), OAuth 2.0 Authentication Pattern (PTN-SEC-API-005), API Versioning Pattern (PTN-APP-API-020), Circuit Breaker Pattern (PTN-APP-API-006), Distributed Tracing Pattern (PTN-INFRA-EVT-004), API Monitoring Pattern (PTN-INFRA-EVT-003).
